claim_scope: Calibrated physical-baseline attestation on Purformance HTE 2K-PUR lacquer scratch hardness only, normalized feature domain [0,1]^4. Grants no batch-release, qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority. Intervals are marginal not conditional. Phase-1 would require independent wet-lab validation and a cross-formulator dataset.
honest_interpretation: The Guth-Gold reinforced-network physical model (5 physically-interpretable parameters) reaches pooled LOIO R2=0.3345. The paired bootstrap confirms it significantly beats both the constant baseline (Delta-R2 CI excludes 0) and the crosslink-density-only Rule-1 baseline R2=0.0156 (Delta-R2 CI excludes 0): a >20x improvement, so filler reinforcement (matting silica + pigment) plus network/hard-segment stiffening is real, group-safe signal. It is statistically indistinguishable from unstructured linear regression on all 4 features (R2=0.3341) AND from a DEFAULT HistGBM (R2=0.3857; ML-minus-physical Delta-R2 CI INCLUDES 0) -- so out-of-the-box ML carries no advantage over classical composite mechanics here. Only the parent receipt's TUNED HistGBM (R2=0.8555, external to this receipt) clears the physical baseline, quantifying that the extra variance lives in higher-order interactions accessible only to a hyperparameter-tuned tree ensemble, not to additive classical physics or default ML. The hostile-null y-shuffle collapses the physical R2 to <0, confirming the fit is not exchangeability leakage.

physical_model.equation: H = H0*(1 + a*Vernetzung + b*HDI_IPDI)*(1 + 2.5*phi + 14.1*phi^2), phi = cm*Mattierungsmittel + cp*Pigmentpaste
physical_model.fit: scipy.optimize.least_squares (Trust Region Reflective), bounded, per LOIO training fold; deterministic
physical_model.name: Guth-Gold reinforced-network
physical_model.rationale: Network/hard-segment stiffening (Flory 1953; Wicks-Jones-Pappas 2007 Rule 1) multiplied by Einstein-Guth-Gold rigid-filler modulus reinforcement (Guth&Gold 1938; Guth 1945) from the two filler axes (matting silica, pigment paste).

theory_references: Guth & Gold 1938 Phys. Rev. 53:322 (Einstein-Guth-Gold filler reinforcement)
Flory 1953 Principles of Polymer Chemistry (network modulus ~ crosslink density)
Wicks, Jones, Pappas 2007 Organic Coatings 3rd ed. Wiley Ch. 24 (Rule 1)
Efron & Tibshirani 1993 An Introduction to the Bootstrap (percentile CI)
Cordts, Sassmannshausen, Rendel, Klein, Reddemann, Berge 2024 Chem. Mater. (Purformance, Zenodo 13742098)
